faqs.q: How much does a Greyhound cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $1,200–$4,000 for a Greyhound puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Greyhound?
faqs.a: Budget $200–$400 per month for a Greyhound, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Large breeds cost more across every category — food portions, medication doses and professional services all scale with weight.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Greyhound?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($800–1,200), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($800–1,800 per year). Grooming costs are lower for short-coated breeds managed at home.

faqs.q: How much does a Greyhound cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Greyhound are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,500–$5,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Greyhound?
faqs.a: Greyhounds need brushing once or twice per week.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Greyhounds shed a lot?
faqs.a: Greyhounds shed minimally. A weekly brush is usually sufficient.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Greyhound need?
faqs.a: A rubber grooming glove or soft-bristle brush is sufficient for weekly maintenance on the Greyhound's short coat. Add a nail grinder and ear cleaner for a complete grooming kit.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Greyhound?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Greyhounds that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Greyhounds easy to train?
faqs.a: Greyhounds are independent thinkers and can be challenging to train. They respond best to high-value rewards and clear, consistent criteria. A structured puppy class from week one is strongly recommended.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Greyhound?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Greyhounds. Clicker training with precise timing works well to mark the exact moment of correct behaviour. Avoid aversive methods — they increase anxiety and often create secondary behavioural problems.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Greyhound?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Greyhound?
faqs.a: Greyhounds can take longer to reach reliable obedience than easier-to-train breeds — expect 3–6 months of consistent daily training for solid basics. Their independent nature means results compound slowly but durably with patience.

faqs.q: What health problems do Greyhounds commonly have?
faqs.a: Greyhounds are most commonly associated with blood vessel disorders and other breed-specific conditions. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Greyhounds live?
faqs.a: Greyhounds have an average lifespan of 10–13 years. Larger breeds typically have shorter lifespans than smaller breeds. Maintaining a healthy weight and regular vet care are the most impactful factors for longevity.

faqs.q: Are Greyhounds prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Greyhounds have a moderate-to-elevated risk of hip dysplasia, particularly for large or active breeds. Ask for OFA or PennHIP hip evaluation certificates when buying from a breeder. Weight control and avoiding high-impact exercise during bone growth (under 18 months) reduces risk.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Greyhound puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Greyhound puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Greyhound-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Greyhounds good with kids?
faqs.a: Greyhounds are generally known for being friendly and patient, making them well-suited to family life with children. Supervision is always recommended with young children regardless of breed — interactions should be taught from both sides.

faqs.q: Do Greyhounds get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Greyhounds can be selective with other dogs due to their independent nature. Early socialisation in puppy classes and controlled on-lead introductions with other dogs help build positive associations.

faqs.q: Do Greyhounds bark a lot?
faqs.a: Greyhounds tend to be vocal — they may bark at strangers, sounds, or when under-stimulated. Adequate daily exercise and mental enrichment (training sessions, puzzle feeders) significantly reduce nuisance barking. Teaching a "quiet" cue early is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Are Greyhounds good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Greyhounds are not ideally suited to apartments — their size and energy level need outdoor space and significant daily exercise. If you do have an apartment, plan for 60–90 minutes of outdoor exercise daily and consider doggy daycare for additional stimulation.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Greyhound need per day?
faqs.a: Greyhounds need approximately 60–90 minutes of exercise daily. Split across at least two sessions daily, with one higher-intensity session (running, fetch, swimming) and one loose-lead sniff walk. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Greyhounds good running partners?
faqs.a: Yes — Greyhounds make excellent running partners once fully grown (typically 12–18 months for medium breeds, 18–24 months for large breeds). Start with shorter distances and build gradually to protect developing joints.

faqs.q: What happens if a Greyhound doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Under-exercised Greyhounds often develop destructive behaviours — chewing, digging, excessive barking, and hyperactivity indoors. These are symptoms of frustration, not bad temperament. Two missed exercise sessions back-to-back typically shows up as restlessness or nuisance behaviour.

faqs.q: Can a Greyhound be off-lead?
faqs.a: Off-lead freedom for a Greyhound depends on recall reliability, not breed alone. Train recall from puppyhood using long-line sessions before progressing to full off-lead. A long-line is recommended as an intermediate step for several months.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Greyhound?
faqs.a: A Greyhound needs approximately 3–5 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Greyhound?
faqs.a: Adult Greyhounds should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds. For large and giant breeds, twice daily feeding also reduces the risk of bloat (GDV) compared to one large daily meal.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Greyhound?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Active Greyhounds benefit from higher-protein formulas (26–30% crude protein) to support muscle maintenance.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Greyhound from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Large breeds should stay on a large-breed puppy formula until 18–24 months, then transition to an adult formula. Switching too early can disrupt joint development during the growth phase.

faqs.q: Is a Greyhound a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Greyhounds can be challenging for first-time owners due to their independent temperament. Prior dog experience or professional training classes from the start significantly improves outcomes. Research the breed thoroughly before committing.

faqs.q: Are Greyhounds good family dogs?
faqs.a: Greyhounds are typically affectionate family dogs that do well with children and adapt to household routines. Their sociable nature means they prefer company over isolation.

faqs.q: Do Greyhounds do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Greyhounds are more independent than many breeds and generally tolerate alone time better than highly social dogs. Still, aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone for an adult dog, and less for puppies.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Greyhound?
faqs.a: Plan for 2–3 hours per day dedicated to your Greyhound — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction.  The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
